key_insight: Boron redistributes toward defects in TiAl, where local pinning of dislocations and suppression of deformation twinning increase resistance to high-temperature plastic deformation.
engineering_relevance: Controlling boron content and defect structure could strengthen TiAl alloys, while requiring attention to brittle borides and their interface adhesion.
method: Developed a high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential.
Combined grand-canonical Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulations.
Analyzed boron redistribution, defect interactions, and deformation mechanisms.
evidence_signal: In simulated polycrystalline TiAl at 900 K, 1 at.% boron increased average flow stress by 9.4% and reduced shear strain accumulation.
watch_item: The strengthening result is simulation-based; experimental validation is needed to assess performance under practical processing and loading conditions.
paper_title: Atomistic insight into defect-mediated boron redistribution and high-temperature strengthening in TiAl alloys
